description.fr-FR: Les huit pièces que Thérèse composa pour les fêtes de sa communauté entre 1894 et 1897 (RP 1–8) : deux sur Jeanne d’Arc, les Anges à la crèche, Jésus à Béthanie, le Divin Petit Mendiant de Noël, la Fuite en Égypte, le Triomphe de l’Humilité et saint Stanislas Kostka. Mêlant dialogues et couplets chantés, elles étaient jouées par les sœurs. Texte authentique de l’édition du Centenaire, d’après les archives du Carmel de Lisieux.
description.en-US: The eight pieces Thérèse composed for her community’s feasts between 1894 and 1897 (RP 1–8): two on Joan of Arc, the Angels at the Crib, Jesus at Bethany, the Divine Little Beggar of Christmas, the Flight into Egypt, the Triumph of Humility, and St Stanislaus Kostka. Mixing dialogue and sung verses, they were performed by the sisters. The authentic text of the Centenary edition, from the archives of the Carmel of Lisieux.
description.pt-BR: As oito peças que Teresinha compôs para as festas da comunidade entre 1894 e 1897 (RP 1–8): duas sobre Joana d’Arc, os Anjos no presépio, Jesus em Betânia, o Divino Pequeno Mendigo do Natal, a Fuga para o Egito, o Triunfo da Humildade e são Estanislau Kostka. Com diálogos e estrofes cantadas, eram representadas pelas irmãs. Texto autêntico da edição do Centenário, segundo os arquivos do Carmelo de Lisieux.

sources.edition: Archives du Carmel de Lisieux, one page per play (/archive/j-m-j-t-la-mission-de-jeanne-darc/, /archive/les-anges-a-la-creche-de-jesus/, /archive/jeanne-darc-accomplissant-sa-mission/, /archive/jesus-a-bethanie/, /archive/le-divin-petit-mendiant-de-noel-demandant-laumone-aux-carmelites/, /archive/la-fuite-en-egypte/, /archive/le-triomphe-de-lhumilite/, /archive/rp-8-saint-stanislas-kostka/), the transcription read from each page's json-cahiers data folio by folio (Nouvelle Édition du Centenaire text).
sources.description: Thérèse's text only. The editors' apparatus is left out: the NEC line numbers (5, 10, 15 …) and stanza numbers printed in the text, the links to the musical scores ("Voir la partition"), and the bracketed notes on leaves Thérèse inserted ("[Ici Thérèse a inséré une feuille volante…]"). Speakers' names are set in bold, stage directions in italics, and runs of verse lines are kept as lines. A sentence that runs over a folio side is joined. Facsimile and score links are not kept.
sources.tierEvidence: Thérèse died in 1897; the plays were first published in 1985 (Récréations pieuses, Cerf), so the 25-year right in posthumous works (CPI art. L123-4) ended in 2010. The site states no terms (its mentions légales page is empty, checked 2026-11-01); the editors' line numbers and notes are not taken.
